newsitem.title: USA: Telephone and Data says election certified.
newsitem.headline: Telephone and Data says election certified.

text.p: Telephone and Data Systems Inc (TDS) said Monday that election inspectors certified that Martin Solomon, nominated to serve on its board by an institutional shareholder, was elected.

The inspectors also certified that two other shareholder proposals were defeated. Proposals were made to eliminate the company's staggered terms for directors and to require a majority of directors be independent, the company said.
It also said that its board of directors passed resolutions increasing the size of the board to 12 from 11 and re-appointed George Off to fill the vacancy.
Off had been management's nominee, but was defeated by Solomon.

Franklin Mutual Advisers Inc, an unit of Franklin Resources Inc, nominated Solomon, claiming the board had failed to maximize value for shareholders. According to a filing earlier this year with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Franklin had a 9.8 percent stake.

"While we are disappointed that management's candidate, George W. Off, was not elected by the common share group, we are pleased to be able to re-appoint him," LeRoy Carlson, president and chief executive, said in a statement.
"I want to assure all TDS shareholders that management and the board of directors will continue to seek to grow shareholder value," he said.
Telephone and Data provides cellular telephone, local telephone, radio paging services and is developing PCS operations.
